record.field: How do I assign a truck to a shipment?
Open the Dispatch Board, tap the shipment, and pick a suggested driver and vehicle.

Open the Dispatch Board and find the shipment under the "Confirmed" filter — these are the loads waiting to be assigned.

Tap the shipment card to expand it. DeployFleet will suggest a ranked list of available drivers and vehicles based on who's free, qualified, and compliant. Tap a suggestion, then tap Confirm.

If DeployFleet blocks the assignment (for example, an expired document or a driver on leave), you'll see the reason and, if you have permission, an option to override with a typed reason.
How do I change the driver on a shipment?
Reassign from the Dispatch Board before the trip departs; afterwards, contact support.

If the shipment hasn't started its trip yet, open it on the Dispatch Board and re-run the assignment — pick a different driver and confirm.

Once a trip has already departed, the driver is locked in for that trip, since it reflects who is actually on the road. If a driver truly can't complete the trip (breakdown, emergency), mark the trip Delayed or Cancelled from the Trip Board and dispatch a fresh shipment with the new driver.
Payslips pull together a driver's pay period, advances, and loan deductions automatically.

Payroll runs through the Payroll Center. For each driver, a payslip is generated for the pay period, and any active loan automatically deducts its instalment when you confirm the payslip.

Driver advances (cash given ahead of pay, for example for fuel on a long trip) are tracked separately and settled against the driver's next payslip.

Payroll and Loans are only visible to users with the Payroll Officer role or the Owner role — this keeps salary information private, the same way it would be in a paper-based office.
Each vehicle has a next-service date or distance; DeployFleet flags it automatically as it approaches.

Every vehicle has a maintenance schedule — either a date (e.g. every 6 months) or an odometer distance (e.g. every 10,000 km), whichever comes first. You can see it on the Maintenance Planner or inside a vehicle's own detail on the Fleet Command Center.

When a vehicle is close to due, it shows up on the Maintenance Planner's attention strip and health cards, so nothing gets missed until it becomes a breakdown.

Once the workshop actually services the vehicle and records it, the "next due" date or distance recalculates automatically from that service date.
Every license, permit, and insurance document has an expiry date DeployFleet watches for you.

Vehicle documents (licenses, permits, roadworthiness certificates, insurance) and driver documents (driving licenses, medical certificates) are logged with an expiry date on the Compliance Center.

Each document shows green (valid), amber (expiring soon), or red (expired) — a quick visual scan tells you what needs renewing this week versus what can wait.

An expired document can also block a vehicle or driver from being assigned to a new shipment, unless a manager explicitly overrides it with a reason.
How do I add a new vehicle to my fleet?
Add it from the Fleet Command Center — plate, model, type, and capacity.

Open the Fleet Command Center and add a new vehicle with its license plate, model, vehicle type, and capacity. It starts out Available, ready to be assigned on the Dispatch Board.

If your fleet uses a vehicle type that doesn't exist yet (for example, a new trailer class), add it first from Vehicle Types — it only takes a few fields.
Where can I see how much a vehicle is costing me?
Fuel logs, load expenses, and workshop costs are all visible per vehicle and fleet-wide.

A single vehicle's fuel, maintenance, and workshop history is on its detail card in the Fleet Command Center. Fleet-wide fuel trends live on Fuel Intelligence, and per-trip costs live on the Load Expense Ledger.

For a money view across the whole business — revenue, outstanding balances, and an approximate margin — see Financial Intelligence.
Usually a status filter, a Scrapped status, or a permissions issue.

Most likely cause: the Fleet Command Center is filtered to a status your truck isn't in — check the status chips (All / Available / Assigned / Maintenance / Breakdown) and tap "All".

Also check: the vehicle may have been marked "Scrapped," which hides it from the active fleet views by design. Ask a manager to check the vehicle's record directly if you believe this happened by mistake.

Permissions: drivers see fewer fleet details than dispatchers and managers. If you're a driver and expect to see full fleet data, that's expected — ask your dispatcher.
DeployFleet blocks unsafe or non-compliant assignments on purpose — the error tells you why.

DeployFleet deliberately stops you from assigning a driver who is unsafe or not compliant to drive right now. The message you see on the Dispatch Board tells you the specific reason, which is usually one of:

  • The driver's license or another required document has expired.
  • The driver is on approved leave during the shipment's pickup date.
  • The driver has already driven too many consecutive days, or hasn't had enough rest between trips.
  • The driver isn't qualified for this vehicle's type.

If the situation genuinely calls for an exception, a manager can override the block with a typed reason — this is recorded permanently in the Compliance Overrides ledger, so it's always visible who approved the exception and why.
A trip only exists once a shipment is confirmed and assigned — check the Dispatch Board first.

A trip is created automatically the moment a shipment's driver and vehicle assignment is confirmed. If you don't see it on the Trip Board, the shipment is probably still sitting unassigned on the Dispatch Board — check there first.

If the trip already completed or was cancelled, the Trip Board's filter chips default to active trips only — switch to "All" to see its full history.

If you're certain a trip was confirmed but genuinely can't find it anywhere, it may have been mistakenly cancelled — check with your dispatcher, since cancellations are visible in the trip's own change history.
Invoicing needs a completed delivery and an active contract with the customer.

An invoice is only created once a shipment has a recorded delivery (proof it actually arrived) — check the Delivery Center to confirm the delivery was logged.

You'll also need an active contract with that customer for DeployFleet to know what rate to charge — a shipment for a customer with no active contract can't price itself automatically. Check Contract & Rate Cards.

If both of those are in place and the invoice still isn't showing, check the Invoice Ledger with the "Draft" filter — it may already exist but not yet be confirmed.
A schedule recalculates rather than disappears — it's usually just no longer due soon.

A maintenance schedule doesn't get deleted when it's serviced — it recalculates its next-due date or distance and drops off the "due soon" attention strip, which can look like it vanished.

Check the Maintenance Planner's Overview tab and look up the vehicle directly in its Health Card — the schedule is still there, just no longer flagged as urgent.

If a vehicle genuinely has no schedule at all, it may be a new vehicle that hasn't had one set up yet — ask a fleet manager to configure it.
What can Copilot do for me?
Ask Copilot questions in plain language — it can look things up, spot risks, and suggest actions.

What Copilot is

Copilot is DeployFleet's built-in AI assistant. It can answer questions about your fleet, flag problems before they become expensive, and — for a small, carefully chosen set of safe actions — take action for you once you approve it.

Try asking it things like

  • "Show vehicles needing maintenance"
  • "Which drivers performed best this month?"
  • "Find overdue invoices"
  • "Why is truck DF-203 consuming more fuel?"

Open Copilot from the tab on the right edge of the screen, or from the Copilot Console for a fuller view with each AI agent's usage and cost.

Approvals — nothing happens without you

When Copilot proposes a change (like reassigning a load), it shows up as a pending approval you review and either approve or reject — Copilot never silently changes your data. A very small number of clearly safe, easy-to-undo actions (like marking an available vehicle available again) may apply immediately, and are always visible afterward.

Reports and analysis

Beyond answering questions, Copilot's agents run in the background to catch things a busy manager might miss — vehicles at rising breakdown risk, fuel usage that doesn't match a truck's normal pattern, and which driver/vehicle pairing is likely to work best for a new shipment.
